extracted.intended_audience: clinical researchers and clinicians who develop, validate, or use measurement instruments and want to assess inter‑rater/intra‑rater reliability and validity
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and empirical examples for evaluating the inter‑rater and intra‑rater reliability and validity of clinical/observational measurement tools using statistics (kappa, ICC, Krippendorff's alpha, etc.), study design features (blinding, training), and interpretation conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohen's kappa (κ) for inter-rater agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the kappa statistic to quantify inter-rater reliability for categorical ratings; kappa values reported for GHAT and SCFT, diagnostic categories, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report κ with interpretation (examples in the text: κ=0.61–0.85 described as substantial to almost perfect; κ=0.36 described as fair). Provide confidence intervals where possible. Note that κ can be low even when percent agreement is moderate if prevalence or bias affects expected agreement. Use when comparing two raters or pairwise agreements; consider weighted kappa for ordered categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weighted kappa (κw) for ordinal scales
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply weighted kappa for ordinal ratings (e.g., tremor rating 0–4 across multiple tests) to account for severity of disagreement between categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report κw and interpret using conventional bands (examples: κw=0.97 described as nearly perfect). Use in multi-category ordinal scales and include examples of subgroup κw (by rater experience).

rubrics_metrics.name: Intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use ICC to assess inter- and intra-rater reliability for continuous or scale scores (examples: ICC=0.82 for RAID-N overall, ICC(3,k) reported for VAS ratings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify ICC model and form (e.g., ICC(2,1), ICC(3,k), two-way mixed). Report ICC with standard errors or confidence intervals. Interpret using conventions (examples in text: ICC=0.82 = good; training effects can increase ICC). Use ICC for averaged measures across raters as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percent agreement / proportions of agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Report crude percentage agreement (overall, positive, negative) between raters as a descriptive measure of concordance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide percent agreements alongside kappa/ICC because percent agreement is intuitive; however, note it does not account for chance agreement. Some studies used thresholds (e.g., more than two‑thirds, 66.7% considered acceptable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevalence- and bias-adjusted kappa and maximum achievable kappa
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculate prevalence- and bias-adjusted kappa and the maximum achievable kappa to understand how prevalence and bias affect κ values (used in phlebitis scales analysis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report adjusted indices when prevalence or bias distort conventional κ. Present observed and expected agreements and consider these adjusted metrics when κ appears paradoxically low despite high percent agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Krippendorff's alpha (KA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Krippendorff's alpha for multirater reliability across categories and time points (example: KA reported 0.17–0.36 for radiographic pattern categorization).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: KA is suitable for any number of raters and different measurement levels; report KA across intervals and investigate training effects on KA (example: KA increased with rater training).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multirater kappa (M‑kappa) and Gwet's AC1
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply multirater extensions of kappa (M‑kappa) and alternative chance‑adjusted agreement statistics like Gwet's AC1 for assessing agreement among multiple raters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use M‑kappa and AC1 alongside KA and percent agreement in multirater settings; present ranges over follow‑up intervals to capture stability over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spearman rank-order correlation for convergent validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Spearman correlation coefficients to assess convergent validity between a new tool and an established measure (example: CSU‑FAPS vs CMPS‑Feline; reported Spearman = 0.31).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define adequacy thresholds a priori (one study considered 0.4–0.8 as adequate). Report p‑values and confidence intervals; discuss whether correlations meet guideline thresholds for validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROC analysis: sensitivity, specificity, AUC and cut-off selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Use receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis to identify optimal cut-off points for screening scales (example: RAID‑N cut‑off ≥12 gave sensitivity 82.1% and specificity 70.0%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report AUC, chosen cut-off, sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy. Justify tradeoffs between sensitivity and specificity based on clinical utility and intended use. Assess performance in the target population.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cronbach's alpha for internal consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Report Cronbach's alpha to evaluate internal consistency of a scale (example: RAID‑N Cronbach's alpha = 0.81).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use alpha to assess scale homogeneity; interpret alongside other validity and reliability metrics. Note alpha depends on number of items and dimensionality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of leave-one-out and other sensitivity analyses for rater variability
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform leave‑one‑out analyses to demonstrate variability contributed by individual raters and to assess robustness of agreement metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report how agreement statistics change when individual raters are removed; use to identify outlier raters or dependence of results on particular raters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Many‑Facet Rasch Model (MFRM) to characterize rater severity and construct difficulty
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply a three‑facet MFRM to estimate reviewer severity/leniency, candidate suitability, and rubric construct difficulty (example: explained variance partitioning in application review study).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use MFRM to separate facets affecting scores (rater, item/construct, candidate). Report variance components and consider MFRM when rater severity differences may bias outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bland–Altman method to assess observer bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Bland and Altman plots/methods to test bias between observers and to quantify mean differences and limits of agreement (example: observer 1 scored 0.41 units above observer 2 with CI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present Bland–Altman plots and statistics to detect systematic biases between raters; interpret whether bias is clinically meaningful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretive categories / classification schemes for reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Use established interpretive schemes (e.g., Altman's classification: very good, good, moderate, fair, poor; or descriptors 'substantial', 'near perfect') when reporting reliability coefficients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the interpretive framework used and apply consistently across metrics. Examples from text: κ or ICC described as 'fair', 'moderate', 'good', 'very good', 'substantial', 'near perfect'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for event/item prevalence and frequency limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that items occurring too infrequently cannot generate reliable κ scores and that prevalence affects agreement metrics (example: 11 items occurred too infrequently to generate kappa).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report item prevalence and consider alternative statistics or pooled categories for rare events. Update instruments/checklists when item availability changes in the environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blinding of raters and use of independent/tiebreaker adjudication
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement blinding of the second rater to the first rater's findings and use independent tiebreakers when discordant (example: second rater blinded; tiebreaker forced patient to choose correct answer).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design studies with blinded raters to reduce bias; define procedures for resolving discordant ratings (third‑party adjudication or consensus). Report blinding procedures explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training, calibration, and use of standardized teaching materials to improve reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide rater training (e.g., teaching videotapes, calibration sessions, endoscopy‑assisted training) to improve inter‑ and intra‑rater reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document training content and duration. Demonstrate post‑training reliability improvements (examples: teaching videotape produced κw≈0.97; calibration training improved κ). Consider refresher training to sustain reliability over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider rater experience and role differences
rubrics_metrics.description: Report and analyze reliability by rater experience or professional role (examples: specialists vs fellows vs generalists; physicians vs nurses vs research assistants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stratify reliability results by rater subgroup, since experience and role often affect agreement. Use targeted training or selection to reduce systematic differences; consider comparing clinical staff vs trained research assistants for data collection accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess both inter‑rater and intra‑rater reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate both inter‑rater (between different raters) and intra‑rater (same rater over time) reliability using appropriate measures (kappa, ICC) and time intervals (example: intra‑rater tested at two‑week intervals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include repeated measures for intra‑rater estimates and specify intervals. Report both components because a tool may show good intra‑rater but poor inter‑rater reliability (or vice versa).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess convergent and content validity alongside reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine validity (content, convergent, predictive) in addition to reliability (examples: content validity claims, convergent validity via correlation with established scales, validity against DSM criteria).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use gold standards or external diagnoses where available (e.g., DSM diagnoses) and report sensitivity/specificity, AUC, and correlation coefficients. Note that good reliability does not guarantee validity; present both.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report study design and sample characteristics that affect reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide sample size, subject characteristics, number of raters, rater blinding, and follow‑up intervals because these influence reliability estimates (examples: 60 subjects, 8 raters, 6 raters scoring serial CTs, 21 cats by 4 raters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about study populations, sampling (e.g., equal numbers with/without condition), and the clinical setting. Discuss generalizability and the need for assessment in different settings and populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multiple agreement metrics and triangulate results
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a suite of agreement statistics (kappa, weighted kappa, ICC, percent agreement, Krippendorff's alpha, Gwet's AC1, adjusted kappa) to capture different aspects of reliability and to avoid misinterpretation from a single statistic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present multiple complementary statistics, explain discrepancies (e.g., low κ but high percent agreement), and choose metrics appropriate to the scale and number of raters. Discuss limitations of each metric in the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider clinical utility and predictive capability, not just statistical reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether a tool's reliability translates into clinical usefulness and ability to predict relevant outcomes (examples: recommendation to evaluate new approaches that predict complications; considerations of clinical utility in SAAIA and other tools).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report whether reliability levels are sufficient for intended clinical decisions. When tools are used for screening or to guide treatment, assess predictive validity and cost/benefit of measurement error.
